missions.name: Annihilation
missions.description: Both players score Victory Points for destroying enemy units. A relentless war of attrition where every kill counts.

scoring.text: At the end of each player turn, score 3VP for each enemy unit that was destroyed during that turn. Score 4VP instead if the destroyed unit had a Power Rating of 11 or more.

mission_rules.name: Marked for Death
mission_rules.text: At the start of the battle, both players secretly mark one enemy unit. If that unit is destroyed, score 5 bonus VP.

missions.tip: Bring high-volume attacks and target elite units for bonus VP. Units with Power Rating 11+ are top priority.

missions.name: Take and Hold
missions.description: Control objective markers to score VP. A classic hold-and-control mission that rewards mobility and board presence.

scoring.text: At the end of each player turn, score 4VP for each objective marker you control. If you control more objective markers than your opponent, score 1 bonus VP.

mission_rules.name: Choke Points
mission_rules.text: Objective markers cannot be placed within 3" of any terrain feature that blocks line of sight.

missions.tip: Units with high OC are critical. Spread across the board early and contest as many objectives as possible.

missions.name: Purge the Foe
missions.description: A dual-scoring mission combining objective control and unit destruction. Rewards aggressive armies that can both hold and kill.

scoring.text: At the end of each player turn, score 3VP for each objective marker you control.
At the end of each battle round, each player scores 4VP if more enemy units than friendly units were destroyed this round.

mission_rules.name: No Mercy, No Respite
mission_rules.text: Each time a unit is destroyed, the controlling player of the unit that destroyed it scores 1 bonus VP (max 10 per player).

missions.tip: Hybrid playstyle required. Prioritise objective control early, switch to hunting for destroy VP once the board is set.

missions.name: Scorched Earth
missions.description: Both players can score or deny VP by burning objective markers — or conserve them for end-of-game control scoring.

scoring.text: At the end of the battle, score 4VP for each objective marker you control.

Once per turn, instead of controlling an objective, a unit can perform the Scorch action. At the end of the action, that objective is Scorched — removed from play. You score 6VP when you Scorch an objective marker your opponent controlled at the start of your turn.

mission_rules.name: Scorched Ground
mission_rules.text: Scorched objective markers are removed from play. No player can score VP from a Scorched objective.

missions.tip: Burn objectives your opponent is about to contest rather than cede them. Timing the Scorch action is the key skill in this mission.

missions.name: Secure Missing Artefacts
missions.description: Recover and secure hidden artefacts scattered across the battlefield. Mobile units with strong actions excel here.

scoring.text: At the start of the battle, place 6 artefact tokens on the battlefield — 2 in each player's deployment zone and 2 in No Man's Land. Each token is Hidden until a unit moves within 3" of it.

A unit can perform the Secure Artefact action if it is within 3" of an artefact token. At the end of the action, remove the token — that player has Secured it. Score 5VP immediately and 3VP at the end of each subsequent turn while the securing unit survives.

mission_rules.name: Hidden Artefacts
mission_rules.text: Artefact tokens are face-down until a unit moves within 3". Some tokens are Decoys — worth 0VP. Only 4 of the 6 tokens are true artefacts.

missions.tip: Fast units like bikes, jump infantry, and aircraft excel at securing artefacts. Protect your unit after securing for the ongoing VP.

missions.name: Sites of Power
missions.description: Channel power through mystical sites using Psykers and Characters. Rewards army lists built around powerful characters.

scoring.text: At the end of each player turn, for each objective marker you control with a CHARACTER or PSYKER unit, score 5VP instead of the standard 3VP.
Objective markers controlled without a CHARACTER or PSYKER score 3VP at the end of each player turn.

mission_rules.name: Power Nexus
mission_rules.text: The central objective marker is worth 2 bonus VP per turn for the player that controls it with a CHARACTER model.

missions.tip: Build your list around durable Characters. Warlords and named characters are especially valuable here.

missions.name: Priority Targets
missions.description: Four objective markers each assigned a priority level. High-priority objectives give bonus VP at the end of the battle.

scoring.text: At the start of the battle, each of the 4 objective markers is randomly assigned a priority: Alpha (6VP end-of-battle), Beta (5VP), Gamma (4VP), Delta (3VP).
At the end of each player turn, score 3VP for each objective marker you control. At the end of the battle, score bonus VP based on which priority objectives you control.

mission_rules.name: Concealed Priorities
mission_rules.text: Priority cards are hidden until the start of Battle Round 3, when all are revealed simultaneously.

missions.tip: Play conservatively early while reading your opponent's movements — then pivot to contest revealed high-priority objectives in Round 3.

missions.name: Deployment Map: Search and Destroy
missions.description: Players deploy in opposite corners of the battlefield. Long diagonal engagement distances favour long-range firepower and fast units.

mission_rules.name: Deployment Zone
mission_rules.text: Each player deploys in a 12" triangle in their corner of the battlefield. No Man's Land is the remaining area.

missions.tip: Fast movement and deep strike units are strong — use them to cross No Man's Land quickly and contest objectives.

missions.name: Deployment Map: Crucible of Battle
missions.description: Standard side-to-side deployment. Both players set up across the long table edges, with a 12" No Man's Land between them.

mission_rules.name: Deployment Zone
mission_rules.text: Each player deploys within 12" of their long table edge.

missions.tip: Balanced deployment for balanced armies. Anvil units hold the line; hammer units push for mid-table objectives.

missions.name: Deployment Map: Dawn of War
missions.description: Both players deploy along the short table edges. Short engagement distances mean fighting starts immediately from Turn 1.

mission_rules.name: Deployment Zone
mission_rules.text: Each player deploys within 12" of their short table edge. This reduces the total No Man's Land distance.

missions.tip: Melee armies love Dawn of War — they get into combat faster. Gunlines need screens and terrain to survive the initial engagement.

missions.name: Deployment Map: Hammer and Anvil
missions.description: Players deploy on opposite short edges with maximum separation — 24" of No Man's Land. Favours shooting armies and units with long range.

mission_rules.name: Deployment Zone
mission_rules.text: Each player deploys within 12" of their short table edge. Maximum 24" separation — longest possible engagement distance.

missions.tip: Long-range shooting dominates here. Melee armies need strong screening and mobility tools to cross safely.

missions.name: Deployment Map: Spearhead Assault
missions.description: One player deploys in a corner, the other in the opposite long edge. Asymmetric deployment creates unique flanking opportunities.

mission_rules.name: Deployment Zone
mission_rules.text: One player deploys in a 12" corner zone; the other deploys along the opposite long table edge within 6". Asymmetric but balanced at scale.

missions.tip: The spearhead player should push aggressively into No Man's Land. The long-edge player should hold flanks and react to the thrust.
